newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's conservatives inch into lead - poll.
newsitem.headline: Austria's conservatives inch into lead - poll.

text.p: Austria's conservative People's Party has snatched the lead from Chancellor Franz Vranitzky's Social Democrats ahead of European parliamentary elections on Sunday, an opinion poll said on Wednesday.

In the poll conducted by research institute Market for the newspaper Der Standard, 31 percent of Austrians said they would vote for the party of Vice Chancellor Wolfgang Schuessel, edging the Social Democrats into second place with 30 percent.
The far-right Freedom Party of populist Joerg Haider came in third with 23 percent of votes, while the Greens and the Liberal Forum each received eight percent, the poll said.
However, nearly half of those questioned said they had yet to decide for which party to vote.

Some 5.8 million citizens are eligible to vote in the October 13 election, the first European parliament vote since Austria joined the EU in January last year. Those elected will sit until a Europe-wide vote in June 1999.
